opening: I keep getting these awful headaches. Sometimes I see shimmering lights before the pain starts.
questions: What do you see before the headache starts?
It starts as a tiny flickering zigzag. It spreads slowly across my vision, then fades away after about twenty-five minutes.
What is the headache like afterward?
Usually one side of my head throbs. I feel sick and even normal light bothers me.
Has this happened before?
Yes, I have had similar episodes for years. They follow more or less the same sequence.
Does the visual disturbance arrive all at once?
No, it builds up over several minutes rather than appearing suddenly.

opening: By the end of a long day, it feels like someone has tightened a band around my head.
questions: Where exactly do you feel the pain?
It is on both sides, more like a tight band than a pounding pain.
When do you tend to notice it?
Mostly toward the end of long working days.
Does being active make it worse?
Not particularly. I can usually keep moving around, although it is unpleasant.
Do you also vomit or see flashing lights beforehand?
No, neither of those happens with these headaches.

opening: Yesterday I noticed the right side of my face was not moving properly. I cannot even close that eye all the way.
questions: What did you notice when you looked in the mirror?
The right side of my mouth would not move properly, and I could not shut my right eye all the way.
How quickly did it happen?
It developed over about eighteen hours.
Can you still raise your eyebrow on that side?
Not normally. The whole right side of my face feels weak.
Have your arm or speech been affected?
No, my arms feel normal and I have not noticed trouble speaking.

opening: My hand keeps going numb at night, especially these fingers. I wake up having to shake it out.
questions: Which fingers feel strange?
My thumb, index finger and middle finger go tingly.
Is it worse at any particular time?
It often wakes me up at night.
Does anything make it better?
Shaking my hand seems to settle it for a while.
Do you mainly feel it in the little finger?
No, that is not where I notice it.

opening: I have felt really low for weeks. Things I used to enjoy just do not interest me anymore.
questions: How has your mood been recently?
For about seven weeks I have felt low almost every day. Things I used to enjoy don't feel enjoyable.
What has changed about your sleep and concentration?
I have been sleeping badly, and it is really difficult to stay focused at work.
What thoughts go through your mind about yourself?
I keep feeling guilty, even about things that are not really my fault.
Have you ever had periods when you needed very little sleep and felt unusually energized?
No, I have not experienced anything like that.

opening: Out of nowhere my heart starts racing and I feel sure something terrible is happening.
questions: What happens when an attack starts?
Out of nowhere my heart starts racing, I shake, and I genuinely think I might die.
Are the attacks tied to one particular place?
No. That is part of what makes them frightening; I can't predict when one will come.
How do you feel between attacks?
I spend a lot of time worrying about when the next one will happen.
How long has that worry been going on?
For around two months now.

opening: My mind is always running through everything that could go wrong. I cannot switch it off.
questions: What do you find yourself worrying about?
Everything: money, work, family. I jump from one problem to another.
Can you put those worries aside?
I try, but my mind just won't let them go.
How long has this been happening?
Most days for around nine months.
Does the worrying affect you physically?
I am tense and restless, and it is difficult to sleep.

opening: I have become noticeably slower, and one of my hands shakes when I am sitting still.
questions: What first made you think something had changed?
One of my hands began shaking when it was resting. It came on gradually.
Has anything changed about your writing?
My handwriting has become noticeably smaller.
What about walking?
I have noticed that one arm does not swing as much when I walk.
Did all of these changes happen suddenly?
No, it has been gradual.

opening: My hands shake whenever I try to hold a cup or do something precise.
questions: When do your hands shake most?
When I hold a cup or try to use my hands, not mainly when they are sitting still.
Is it the same on both sides?
Yes, both hands are involved.
How long have you noticed this?
Around eight years.
Have you also become unusually slow or stiff?
No, I haven't noticed anything like that. Stress definitely makes the shaking worse, though.

opening: My family says I keep asking the same questions. I am finding everyday things harder to remember.
questions: What sorts of things are becoming harder to remember?
I ask the same questions again and misplace things, even after someone has explained where they are.
How long has this been changing?
It has been getting gradually worse over about three years.
Are everyday tasks affected?
I now need help keeping track of bills and finances.
Did this begin overnight?
No. It has been a slow change rather than one sudden event.

opening: Ever since the strokes, thinking things through takes me longer, and some days feel like a step backward.
questions: Did the thinking problems begin all at once?
They seemed to worsen in steps, particularly after my strokes.
What is most difficult day to day?
Planning and organizing things is harder than remembering a particular conversation.
Do you have any cardiovascular health problems?
I have high blood pressure and have had strokes before.
Has there been a steady decline without interruptions?
Not really. There have been clearer drops in ability at different times.

opening: Some days I seem quite clear, but other days I get confused. I have even seen people who were not there.
questions: Are the difficulties the same throughout the day?
Not at all. Sometimes I am quite alert, and other times I seem much more confused.
Have you noticed anything unusual in your surroundings?
I sometimes see people who aren't actually there. They look surprisingly detailed.
What happens while you are asleep?
My family says I move around and act out dreams.
Was memory loss the first big concern?
No, the changes in alertness and these strange experiences were noticeable early on.

opening: My family says I am acting like a different person and making decisions I would never have made before.
questions: Have the changes mostly been about forgetting things?
Not really. My family says I behave differently and no longer notice when I hurt someone's feelings.
How has your motivation changed?
I have become much more indifferent about things I used to care about.
Have your eating habits changed?
Apparently I stick rigidly to particular foods and routines now.
When did your family start noticing?
These changes have developed over roughly two years.

opening: My vision and balance have been strange at different times. The symptoms seem to come and go.
questions: Have you had an earlier episode like this?
About nine months ago I lost vision in one eye and it hurt. It eventually improved.
What has happened more recently?
Now I am having problems with sensation and walking.
Did the visual problem and walking problem start together?
No, they were separate episodes months apart.
Has the new trouble come on instantly?
No, it has developed over days rather than within a few seconds.

opening: My eyelids get droopy and my muscles tire out, especially later in the day.
questions: When do your eyelids start drooping?
They are usually better earlier in the day and droop more when I am tired.
What happens to your vision?
I sometimes see double, especially after I have been using my eyes a lot.
Does resting change anything?
Yes. Taking a break usually helps.
Is the weakness exactly the same all day?
No, it comes and goes depending on how much I have been doing.

opening: My feet started tingling, and now my legs feel weaker than they did a few days ago.
questions: When did the weakness begin?
Over the last four days, and it has been getting worse.
What happened in the week before this?
I had a stomach bug with diarrhea about a week before the weakness started.
Where do you feel it?
It is on both sides, with weakness and tingling that have been spreading.
Are you finding it progressively harder to walk?
Yes. It is changing quickly, which is why I am worried.

opening: Sometimes I get this intense feeling that I have lived the moment before, and then I lose track of what happened.
questions: What is the very first thing you notice during an episode?
A sudden feeling of déjà vu, sometimes with a strange rising feeling in my stomach.
What does someone else notice?
I've been told I go blank for a while and make movements with my lips.
Can you remember everything afterward?
No, there is part of it I cannot recall.
How long is a typical episode?
Usually about a minute, and the episodes tend to follow the same pattern.

opening: All of a sudden I could not move one side properly. Everything changed in a moment.
questions: When was the patient last speaking and moving normally?
About forty-five minutes ago. Everything changed very suddenly.
What changed first?
They suddenly couldn't get the words out and the right arm became weak.
Has the weakness already completely passed?
No, the symptoms are still present.
Can this wait for a routine appointment?
No. This has just happened and the person needs emergency assessment now.

opening: For a short while I could not speak properly, but then it seemed to go away.
questions: How long did the language problem last?
About twelve minutes, then it completely cleared.
Did it begin gradually over several hours?
No, it was sudden.
Are you back to your usual self now?
Yes, but it was very frightening.
Do you have risk factors for circulation problems?
Yes, I do have vascular risk factors, which is why the episode worries me.

opening: I hit my head, and since then I have felt foggy and not quite myself.
questions: What happened just before the headache started?
I took a hit to the head while playing sport.
How have you felt since?
I have a headache and my thinking feels a little slower than usual.
Have you noticed weakness in one part of your body?
No, nothing like that.
Have the symptoms been getting rapidly worse?
No, so far there has been no worsening warning sign, but I know I still need assessment.

opening: I know the thoughts do not make sense, but I cannot stop checking things.
questions: What thought keeps bothering you?
I keep imagining that the stove is going to start a fire, even when I know I switched it off.
What do you do when that thought comes up?
I go back and check it, sometimes again and again.
How much time does it take?
Around two hours on some days. It is exhausting.
Does the checking feel completely reasonable to you?
No. I know it is excessive, but I still feel driven to do it.

opening: Since what happened, I keep reliving it, and I avoid anything that reminds me.
questions: What sorts of memories are troubling you?
Memories of the trauma keep pushing into my mind when I don't want them.
Do you try to avoid reminders?
Yes. I go out of my way to avoid things that bring it back.
How has this changed the way you feel day to day?
I am on edge a lot and my mood has changed. It affects my everyday life.
How long have these symptoms lasted?
About four months.

opening: There have been times when I barely slept but felt incredibly energized and unstoppable.
questions: How have you been sleeping lately?
Very little, but I still seem to have plenty of energy.
Has anyone noticed a change in the way you talk?
People keep telling me I talk much faster than usual.
Have you made any unusual decisions?
I have been spending money impulsively and it has caused serious problems.
How long has this unusually energized mood lasted?
About a week, and it is affecting my life a lot.

opening: I get so anxious about being judged that I avoid speaking up or meeting people.
questions: What situations make you most anxious?
Speaking up in class and being around other people who might judge me.
What are you worried they will think?
That I will embarrass myself or say something stupid.
What do you do to cope with it?
I avoid those situations whenever I can, even when it affects my studies.
Has this only been happening for a few weeks?
No, it has been going on for about two years.

opening: I lose track of tasks all the time, even when I am trying very hard to concentrate.
questions: When did you first have problems with attention?
Even in primary school I was losing things and forgetting what I was supposed to do.
Is it just an issue at school?
No. It happens at home too.
What tends to happen when you try to finish tasks?
I get distracted or lose track of the materials I need.
Has this caused real difficulties?
Yes, it has affected how I manage things in more than one setting.

opening: I have been hearing things other people do not seem to hear, and it is frightening.
questions: What has felt different lately?
I have felt watched and threatened, and sometimes I hear voices that other people don't hear.
What has your family noticed?
They say I have become harder to follow when I talk and that I have stopped functioning as I used to.
How long has this been going on?
For around eight months now.
Do these experiences only happen during a period of very high or very low mood?
No. There has not been a sustained mood episode that explains them.

opening: After taking stimulants, I started feeling watched and hearing things.
questions: Was there a change in your treatment before the symptoms started?
Yes. My prescribed stimulant dose was increased shortly before I began feeling watched.
What kinds of experiences are frightening you?
I have become convinced people are after me, even though others say there is no evidence.
Did you have episodes like this before the dose change?
No, I had not experienced this kind of problem before.
Did the symptoms start long before the stimulant was changed?
No, the timing was close to the dose increase.

opening: I have had serious changes in my mood, but the unusual experiences have sometimes happened outside those episodes.
questions: Do the unusual perceptions happen only when you are depressed?
No. I have heard things even when I was not experiencing a major mood episode.
Can you remember a period of psychotic symptoms without mood symptoms?
Yes, there was a stretch of about three weeks like that.
Have you also had serious depressive episodes?
Yes, and they have taken up much of the overall illness.
Has this been just one short episode?
No. It has been going on over years.

opening: Everything became confusing very suddenly. My family says I am not acting like myself.
questions: When did the confusion begin?
It came on recently, after an infection and some medication changes.
Is the person's alertness the same throughout the day?
No, it goes up and down quite a lot.
Was their thinking like this months ago?
No. This is a noticeable change from their usual state.
What other health problem happened around the same time?
There was a urinary infection, and the medicines were also adjusted.

opening: I am walking differently, I have trouble holding my bladder, and my thinking has slowed down.
questions: What has changed about the way you walk?
Starting to walk feels oddly difficult, as though my feet will not get going.
Have you noticed changes in thinking?
I feel slower in my thinking than before.
Any urinary symptoms?
Yes, I have more urgency than I used to.
How long has this combination been developing?
Roughly a year.

opening: My muscles have been getting weaker, and I have started noticing twitching.
questions: Which part of your body first felt weak?
It began in one hand, then I started noticing weakness in a leg as well.
How long has this been progressing?
For about ten months.
Do your hands or feet feel numb?
No, I haven't had the kind of tingling or numbness people ask me about.
Has this been an abrupt episode?
No, it has been steadily getting worse.

opening: My hands feel clumsy and my walking is not as steady as it used to be.
questions: What is difficult to do with your hands?
Small movements have become clumsy. Things that used to be easy take more effort.
How is your balance?
I feel unsteady when I walk.
Have you noticed anything in your neck?
It feels stiff as well.
How long has this developed?
It has crept up over months.

opening: I have a terrible headache and fever, and my neck is so painful to move.
questions: What symptoms developed first?
A severe headache and fever, and then my neck became stiff.
Does light bother you?
Yes, bright light is uncomfortable.
Is the person getting better or more unwell?
More unwell, and quite quickly.
Would you feel safe simply waiting at home?
No. I feel very ill and need urgent medical help.

opening: I suddenly got the worst headache I have ever felt.
questions: How quickly did the headache reach its worst?
Almost instantly. It was at full force within seconds.
What were you doing when it happened?
I was exercising.
What other symptoms followed?
I vomited and my neck hurts.
Does this feel like your usual headache pattern?
No. It was sudden and completely different.

opening: I have been unsteady and confused, and people say my eyes are moving strangely.
questions: Has eating been difficult lately?
Yes, I have hardly been eating properly and I have been vomiting.
Is alcohol part of the history?
Yes, there has been heavy alcohol use.
What has changed about your balance?
I am unusually unsteady when I try to walk.
Are you feeling mentally clear?
No, I have been confused recently.

opening: My feet feel numb and my balance has been getting worse.
questions: What do you notice in your feet?
I have had tingling for months.
Is walking harder in particular conditions?
Yes, especially in the dark when I cannot see where my feet are going.
Has anyone checked your sense of vibration or position?
I was told those sensations were reduced when I was examined.
Did this all happen in a single day?
No, it has developed gradually.

opening: I am having real trouble moving, but the tests so far have not explained why.
questions: What does the weakness feel like to you?
It is real and it gets in the way of what I am trying to do.
Does it always feel exactly the same?
No, it seems to change from one moment to another.
What happens during the examination?
The weakness behaves differently depending on how it is tested, which has confused me.
Does this mean you are pretending?
Absolutely not. I cannot simply choose to make the symptoms disappear.

opening: My family says my behavior changed quickly, and I have had some very strange episodes.
questions: What did your family first notice?
They say I was behaving very differently and seemed confused about things I would normally remember.
Has anything happened besides the changes in behavior?
Yes. There have been seizures and strange movements.
How quickly has this developed?
Over about two weeks.
Could this safely be treated as an ordinary psychiatric appointment?
No. The seizures and rapid change mean I need medical assessment urgently.

opening: My eyesight became very poor and then I developed weakness and other nerve symptoms.
questions: Have you had more than one episode of trouble seeing?
Yes, I've had severe episodes affecting my vision.
Have you also had problems with your legs or bladder?
Yes, I've had prolonged symptoms affecting my spinal cord and bladder control.
Did it all resolve after one brief episode?
No, there have been recurrent, significant attacks.
Are the eye symptoms mild and painless?
No, the episodes have been severe.

opening: My memory and movements have deteriorated incredibly quickly.
questions: How quickly have the thinking problems developed?
Over weeks to months, much faster than anyone expected.
How has walking changed?
I am much less coordinated.
Have there been unusual jerking movements?
Yes, sudden jerks that I cannot control.
Was the decline spread over many years?
No, it has been unusually rapid.

opening: I keep falling, and looking up and down is becoming difficult.
questions: What first brought you to attention?
I kept falling without an obvious reason.
Is turning your gaze downward difficult?
Yes, looking down has become much harder.
Do you feel stiff?
Especially through my trunk and neck.
Did the falls only begin very late?
No, they were among the early problems.

opening: I have problems with balance and blood pressure, and my movements have slowed.
questions: What happens when you stand up?
I become very lightheaded, and I've been told my blood pressure drops badly.
Have you noticed urinary changes?
Yes, those problems began quite early.
What about movement?
I have become slower and stiffer, and things have progressed quite rapidly.
Did the bladder and blood pressure problems appear only years later?
No, they were early features.

opening: I cannot control some of these movements, and my family has noticed changes in my thinking.
questions: What movements have changed?
My arms and legs sometimes make these jerky, dance-like movements that I can't fully control.
Have you noticed changes in thinking?
Planning and keeping track of things have become harder.
Does anyone in your family have a similar condition?
Yes, one of my parents has been affected.
Have your emotions or mood changed too?
Yes, I've noticed mood changes along with everything else.

opening: I fall asleep without meaning to, even when I have had a full night in bed.
questions: What happens during the daytime?
I suddenly get so sleepy that I struggle to stay awake, even when I am trying.
What happens when you laugh or feel strong emotions?
My knees sometimes buckle, but I stay aware of what is happening.
Have you had anything unusual around falling asleep or waking up?
Yes, sometimes I wake up and can't move for a moment.
Are these sleep episodes rare?
No, they're happening every day.

opening: I have a new headache around my temples, and chewing sometimes makes my jaw ache.
questions: Is this a headache you have had for years?
No, it is a new pain around one temple.
Does your scalp feel different?
It is tender to touch.
What happens when you chew?
My jaw starts aching when I chew for a while.
Have you noticed any change in vision?
Yes, it has blurred briefly. That really worries me.

opening: I can still remember things, but I increasingly cannot find the meaning of ordinary words.
questions: What happens when someone says a familiar word?
Sometimes I recognize the sound of the word but don't understand what it means anymore.
Is it hard to name objects?
Yes, even ordinary things that I know I've seen before.
Does your speech come out haltingly?
No, I can still speak fluently; finding the meaning is the problem.
Are your memories of recent events equally affected?
Not nearly as much, at least early on.

opening: My relationships feel intense and unstable, and I am terrified people will leave me.
questions: What tends to happen in close relationships?
I can feel extremely close to someone and then become terrified they're going to leave me.
How do you see yourself?
My sense of who I am seems to change depending on what is happening.
Have you made decisions you later regretted?
Yes, sometimes I act impulsively when I'm overwhelmed.
Is this a recent change after one difficult week?
No, these patterns have been with me since my teens and affect different parts of my life.

opening: I am very afraid of gaining weight, and food has become something I constantly worry about.
questions: What happens when you think about gaining weight?
The idea frightens me intensely, even when other people are worried about how little I eat.
Have you been limiting what you eat?
Yes, I restrict my food a lot.
How do you see your body?
The way I see my body doesn't seem to match what other people tell me.
Has this affected your physical health?
Yes, my weight is too low for what would be expected in my situation.

opening: I make movements and sounds that I feel I have to let out, even when I try not to.
questions: What movements have you noticed?
I make repeated movements I don't always feel I can stop.
Are there also sounds or noises?
Yes, I have vocal tics as well as movements.
When did this start?
When I was about eight years old.
Is it exactly the same every day?
No, the tics come and go in intensity, but they've been present for more than eighteen months.

opening: I have these physical symptoms that worry me constantly, even after medical visits.
questions: Do you feel that the physical pain is real?
Yes, very much so. It isn't something I'm imagining.
How much time do you spend thinking about your health?
An enormous amount. I keep checking and worrying about the symptoms.
Have the worries changed your routines?
They take up a lot of my time and energy.
Does this mean every symptom has a clear medical explanation already?
No. I know the cause is not completely clear, but the pain and distress are very real.

opening: My headache has been getting worse, and now I have other neurological symptoms.
questions: How has the headache been changing?
It has been getting worse over days rather than arriving as one sudden flash.
Has anything else happened recently?
I have had a new seizure.
Is there any relevant recent health history?
I was pregnant recently.
Has anyone noticed signs of raised pressure around the eyes?
At the examination they mentioned swelling at the back of my eyes.

opening: I have been feeling unwell, and my movements and mood have changed.
questions: What has changed about your movements?
I have a tremor and sometimes my muscles twist into awkward positions.
Have your mood or behavior changed?
Yes, people around me have noticed changes.
Has anything unusual shown up in blood tests?
I was told my liver tests were abnormal.
Is this only a problem with the liver?
No, the movement and psychological changes are also part of what brought me here.

opening: I have felt down for such a long time that I can barely remember feeling different.
questions: How long have you felt low?
For about four years, most days.
Do you have long periods when you feel completely fine?
No. I haven't had a break longer than a couple of months.
What does it feel like day to day?
I'm tired, hard on myself, and often expect the worst.
Has it affected your life?
Yes, it's more than just a gloomy mood now and then.

opening: I have had deep depressive periods, but also times when I felt unusually energized.
questions: What happens during the periods when your energy changes?
For about four days at a time I become much more energetic and social and need less sleep.
Have those periods been as disruptive as a full manic episode?
No, they've been noticeable changes, but not to that degree.
What happens at other times?
I've also had several significant depressive episodes.
Have you ever had a full episode of mania?
No, not according to the history I've described.

opening: My mood seems to swing between being low and unusually upbeat, over and over.
questions: Do your moods stay steady for long stretches?
Not really. I have repeated times when I'm a bit too energized and other times when I'm low.
How long has that been happening?
About three years.
Do these phases meet the threshold of full manic or major depressive episodes?
I've been told the individual phases fall short of that, even though the pattern affects me.
Have there been long symptom-free gaps?
No, not long ones.

opening: I avoid places where I worry I could not escape or get help.
questions: Which places feel especially hard to enter?
Trains, busy shops, crowds, queues, or even going outside alone.
What frightens you about those places?
I'm afraid I won't be able to get out or get help if I panic or feel unwell.
Do you avoid them?
Yes, sometimes I change my plans entirely.
How long has this been affecting your life?
About eight months.

opening: I am scared I have a serious disease even when doctors cannot find one.
questions: What are you most worried might be happening?
I'm afraid I have a serious disease, even when I don't have many actual symptoms.
What happens after a reassuring appointment?
I feel better briefly, but then the worry returns.
How long has this been taking over your thoughts?
Around ten months.
Are you mainly distressed by severe ongoing physical symptoms?
No, the fear of what might be wrong is the biggest problem.

opening: There is something about my appearance that I cannot stop thinking about.
questions: What is worrying you about your appearance?
There's something about my face that I can't stop thinking about, even though other people say it's barely noticeable.
What do you do when the worry comes up?
I keep checking mirrors or trying to conceal it.
How much time does it take?
Hours on some days.
Does it interfere with your life?
Yes, I end up avoiding things because I'm so preoccupied.

opening: I cannot bear to throw things away, even when my home is becoming difficult to use.
questions: What makes it hard to throw things away?
Even things with almost no value feel important to keep. I worry I'll need them later.
What is your home like now?
There is so much stuff that the kitchen isn't really usable.
How long has this been happening?
For years; it didn't happen all at once.
Would sorting and discarding the objects feel easy?
No. It causes a great deal of distress.

opening: Sometimes the world feels unreal, almost as though I am watching myself from outside.
questions: What happens during these strange episodes?
It feels as though I'm outside my body or watching myself from a distance.
What happens to familiar places?
Rooms can feel unreal, almost like a film set.
Do you actually believe the room has ceased to exist?
No. I know it's a feeling, even though it is frightening.
How long have these episodes been occurring?
On and off for around eight months.

opening: There are important parts of my life I simply cannot remember.
questions: What part of your memory is missing?
There is a stretch of important personal events that I just can't retrieve.
When did you first notice the gap?
After a period of severe stress.
Can you still learn ordinary new information?
Yes. Everyday things and general knowledge are not missing in the same way.
Is this just forgetting where you put your keys?
No, it involves significant personal experiences.

opening: Ever since the frightening event, I have felt on edge and keep having intrusive memories.
questions: When did the accident happen?
Nine days ago. I witnessed a very serious crash.
What happens when you remember it?
Images come back when I don't want them, and I feel on edge.
Have you changed what you do?
I avoid reminders, and sometimes I feel disconnected from what's happening.
Is it affecting everyday functioning?
Yes, more than I expected for the time since it happened.

opening: Social situations and changes in routine have always been difficult for me.
questions: Were these social differences present only recently?
No, they've been noticeable since childhood.
What kinds of social situations are difficult?
The back-and-forth of conversations and reading other people's social signals can be hard.
Are routines important to you?
Very. Sudden changes can be uncomfortable, and I get deeply absorbed in particular interests.
Do these differences matter in more than one setting?
Yes, they have affected different parts of everyday life.

opening: I have trouble sitting still, staying focused, and finishing things.
questions: Have you struggled to stay focused since childhood?
Yes, I've had attention problems since primary school.
Do you also find yourself acting or speaking before thinking?
Yes, restlessness and impulsive behavior are part of it too.
Does this happen in different places?
At home and in education, not just during one subject.
Has it actually affected your functioning?
Yes, that's why I wanted help.

opening: I want to connect with people, but I am so afraid of rejection that I hold back.
questions: Would you like closer friendships?
Yes, very much. I just worry people will reject me if I try.
What stops you from taking opportunities?
I imagine being criticized or embarrassed and then back away.
Has this affected work or relationships?
Both. I avoid applying for things and getting close to people.
How long has this pattern been present?
Since around late adolescence.

opening: I need things done exactly right, and it is hard to delegate or relax my standards.
questions: What is hardest about delegating tasks?
I worry they won't be done exactly the right way, so I take them back or keep checking.
Does planning take more time than doing?
Sometimes I spend so long on rules and details that I miss deadlines.
Where does this show up?
At work and at home.
Is it just one temporary stressful period?
No, I've been this rigid for a long time.

opening: Sometimes I eat far more than I intend to and then try to undo it.
questions: What happens during an eating episode?
I eat much more than I meant to and feel unable to stop.
What do you do afterward?
I sometimes make myself vomit because I'm so afraid of gaining weight.
How often has this pattern occurred?
At least weekly over the last four months.
How does it affect the way you see yourself?
My shape and weight have an enormous influence on how I feel about myself.

opening: I sometimes eat a large amount very quickly and feel out of control afterward.
questions: What are the eating episodes like?
I eat very quickly, even when I'm not physically hungry, and feel I can't stop.
How do you feel afterward?
Ashamed and upset about what happened.
How often does this occur?
At least weekly, for roughly six months.
Do you regularly vomit or use other compensatory behaviors afterward?
No, that isn't part of this pattern.

opening: Eating is hard for me, but not because I want to lose weight.
questions: Why is the range of foods you eat so limited?
Certain textures make me feel sick, and I'm frightened of unpleasant consequences from eating some foods.
Has this been going on long?
Since childhood.
Is the restriction about wanting to change your body shape?
No, it's about how food feels and what I fear will happen.
Has it affected your health?
Yes, I've developed nutritional problems.

opening: I lie awake for hours, and the lack of sleep is affecting my days.
questions: What happens when you try to sleep?
I lie awake for a long time or wake up and can't get back to sleep.
Do you have enough time available for sleep?
Yes, I give myself the opportunity, but sleep still doesn't come easily.
How many nights a week is this a problem?
At least three nights most weeks, for about five months.
What does it do to your daytime life?
I'm tired and it affects how I function during the day.

opening: Drinking has started to control my routine, even though it is causing problems.
questions: Do you sometimes drink more than you planned?
Yes, I tell myself I'll have a little and end up drinking much more.
Have you tried reducing it?
Many times, but I haven't been able to stick to it.
What happens if you think about not drinking?
I get strong cravings.
Has alcohol caused problems outside drinking itself?
Yes, at work and in my relationships, and it's been going on for over a year.

opening: I have a hard time trusting people. I often think they have hidden motives.
questions: What tends to happen when someone makes an ordinary remark?
I often think there's a hidden insult or threat in it.
Is it easy for you to trust other people?
No, I keep wondering whether they're secretly against me.
Does this lead to conflict?
I can hold on to grievances for a long time.
When did this pattern start?
It's been part of how I relate to people since early adulthood.

opening: I generally prefer being alone and do not feel much need for close relationships.
questions: How much do you want close relationships?
Not very much. I've usually been more comfortable alone.
What activities do you choose?
Mostly solitary ones.
Do strong emotional reactions come easily?
I don't tend to show much outward emotion.
Has this only started during a recent depressive episode?
No, it's a longstanding pattern going back to late adolescence.

opening: I often feel that ordinary things have a special meaning just for me.
questions: How do social situations feel to you?
Even with familiar people, I feel uncomfortable and separate from them.
Have other people commented on how you speak?
Yes, they say my speech or ideas can seem unusual.
Do you sometimes find events have a special connection to you?
Sometimes ordinary events seem personally meaningful in an odd way.
Has this been happening for a short time?
No, it's been a pattern over many years.

opening: I have repeatedly gotten into trouble for things that other people say hurt them.
questions: Have you often done things that harmed other people?
I've lied or acted recklessly even when it affected others.
Have there been repeated problems respecting other people's rights?
Yes, across different situations.
Was there evidence of problems before adulthood?
Records and people who knew me then describe conduct problems before I was fifteen.
Is this based on just one isolated incident?
No. It's a longer pattern.

opening: I feel invisible unless people notice me, and my emotions can get very intense.
questions: How do you feel when you are not getting attention?
I can feel uncomfortable, as though I'm fading into the background.
What do people notice about the way you express emotions?
They say I can be very dramatic and expressive.
Does this happen only with one person?
No, it comes up in different social and work settings.
Has this been a recent change?
No, it's how I've been for years.

opening: I need people to recognize what I have achieved, and criticism hits me hard.
questions: What do you hope people notice about you?
I want them to recognize how much I contribute, and it hurts when they don't.
How do disagreements tend to go?
I can become defensive when I feel criticized.
What do others say is difficult about your relationships?
They say I expect special treatment and don't always take their feelings into account.
Is this limited to one recent conflict?
No, it's a pattern in different settings over a long time.

opening: I find it very difficult to make decisions without someone reassuring me.
questions: What is hardest about making an important decision?
I feel I need someone else to reassure me before I can decide.
What happens if you disagree with someone close?
I often stay quiet because I'm afraid they'll stop supporting me.
Have you relied on others like this for a long time?
Yes, across many parts of my life.
Does the possibility of being left alone worry you?
Very much. It affects what I agree to do.

opening: I have been experiencing unusual beliefs and voices, and it has affected my life recently.
questions: When did you start hearing or seeing things others couldn't?
About eight weeks ago.
What else changed around the same time?
My thoughts and speech have become confused, and I've developed beliefs others say are untrue.
Have you had these symptoms for many years?
No, this is a fairly recent episode.
Has a medication or medical illness been identified as the cause?
Not from what has been established in this case.

opening: Something very strange happened to my thinking quite suddenly, and people around me became concerned.
questions: How did the changes begin?
Very suddenly. I started hearing things and my speech became disorganized.
How long did they last?
About twelve days.
How are you functioning now?
I've returned to the way I was before the episode.
Were mood symptoms or substances identified as the explanation?
No, they were not considered the cause in this case.

opening: I am certain someone is acting against me, although others insist I am mistaken.
questions: What do you believe has been happening?
For months I've believed someone is targeting me, even though other people disagree.
How long has this belief been there?
Around seven months.
What is daily life like outside this concern?
Most parts of my everyday life are relatively unchanged.
Have you also had broad disorganization in speech or behavior?
No, that's not what has been described.

opening: These strange experiences began while I was dealing with another medical problem.
questions: Did anything physical change before the unusual experiences?
Yes, I began having seizures and other neurological problems around the same time.
What kinds of mental experiences followed?
I started having experiences and beliefs that worried the people around me.
Did the medical tests find anything relevant?
The workup identified a neurological condition that could explain the new symptoms.
Was there a long history of unexplained psychosis before the neurological changes?
No, this was a new problem alongside the medical changes.

opening: I have been severely depressed and started believing terrible things that others say are not true.
questions: How have you been feeling lately?
Deeply low. Nothing seems enjoyable and everything takes enormous effort.
What kinds of beliefs have troubled you?
I have fixed beliefs about my guilt and worthlessness that people say are not true.
When do those beliefs occur?
Only during this severe depressive episode.
Have you had a period of mania?
No, none has been described in the case history.

opening: During periods when my mood becomes extremely elevated, I have also had unusual beliefs.
questions: How much sleep have you needed?
Almost none for days, yet I still feel unusually energized.
What has changed in your mood and activity?
For about nine days I've been much more elevated or irritable, and I can't slow down.
Have your beliefs changed during this period?
Yes, I have developed beliefs others say are far outside reality while I've been in this state.
How serious has the episode become?
It has disrupted my life so much that hospital care has been needed.
